body:
[A10] Found by the independent review of PR #69 (comment on that PR): `syn/ooc/engine_ooc.tcl` and `syn/ooc/ucpu_ooc.tcl` issue `create_clock` after `synth_design`, so the worst-slack figure the OOC recipe reports is a post-hoc timing report on an unconstrained synthesis. Deltas between two runs of the same script remain comparable (both columns are unconstrained the same way), but the absolute slack (2.249 ns engine, 1.941 ns micro-CPU at 10 ns) must not be read as a constrained result.

Acceptance:
- [ ] The clock constraint is applied before `synth_design` (an XDC read before synthesis, or `create_clock` in a constraints file the script sources first), for both tops.
- [ ] `make ooc` still produces the six retained reports; the utilization and timing figures at the current main are re-measured once with the constrained flow and recorded here beside the unconstrained ones, so the guide's numbers can be re-baselined truthfully.
- [ ] `docs/HDL_DEVELOPER.md` (and wherever the dated resource figures are quoted) states which flow produced the numbers.

Pre-existing at main 6e6237f4; not introduced by PR #69.
title: OOC scripts constrain the clock after synth_design, so the reported slack is unconstrained
